1. Introduction to Applied A
1. What is Applied A
Applied Artificial Intelligence (Applied AI) refers to the practical implementation of 
AI techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and data-driven algorithms 
to solve real-world problems.

AI can be divided into two broad categories
Theoretical AI: focuses on developing new algorithms, models, and proofs 
(often in research and academia).
Applied AI: focuses on using existing AI methods to build systems that work 
reliably in real environments
Applied AI bridges the gap between AI theory and real-world impact
Real-World Example: Spam Email Filterin
Spam email filtering uses machine learning models trained on past emails to classify 
new messages as spam or not spam, focusing on accuracy, speed, and scalability 
rather than inventing new algorithms
1. Why Applied AI Matter
Applied AI matters because it converts theoretical intelligence into usable solutions 
that improve efficiency, accuracy, and decision-ma king

3. Supervised Learning in Practic
Unsupervised Learning is a machine learning technique used when the dataset does 
not contain labelled outputs.

Unlike supervised learning, the model is not trained with correct answers. Instead, 
it analyzes the data to identify hidden patterns, similarities, relationships, or unusual 
behaviour on its own
This approach is especially useful in real-world scenarios where labeling large 
amounts of data is time-consuming, costly, or impractical

4. Neural Networks for Real-World Problem
| What are Neural Networks
Neural Networks are a type of machine learning model inspired by the working of 
the human brain.

Just like the human brain is made up of billions of interconnected neurons, a neural 
network is made up of artificial neurons (also called nodes) that are connected to 
each other.

They consist of
Input layer: receives data
Hidden layers: learn patterns and relationships
Output layer: produces prediction
